sources.entry: Build a Twitter Bot with Clojure

summary.title: Build a Twitter Bot with Clojure (Markov chain tweet generator)
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a Clojure project that generates tweets via a Markov chain trained on Edward Lear poems and Wikipedia functional programming text.
takeaways: Set up a Leiningen Clojure project and test it with lein test and lein-test-refresh.
Turn text into a Markov word chain using partition-all, reduce and merge-with with set union.
Walk the chain randomly to generate text, with a 140-character limit and termination on dead ends.
Train the bot by reading text files with clojure.java.io/resource and slurp, merging their chains.
Use with-redefs to make shuffle deterministic in tests.
summary.summary: This is a hands-on tutorial that builds a Clojure Twitter bot which generates tweets from a mashup of Edward Lear's nonsense poems and Wikipedia articles on functional programming. The author walks through creating a Leiningen project, working interactively in Emacs with Cider and the REPL, and building a Markov chain from prefixes and suffixes. Each step is developed test-first with clojure.test, including random walking of the chain with a 140-character cap and training from text files. The page ends before the final tweaking, Heroku deployment, and Twitter hookup mentioned in its introduction.
